units.title: A Gaussian polynomial feature has its actual ambient L² derivative
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure, let γ be its centered standard Gaussian law with identity covariance, and let p be any finite real polynomial. For every ambient w and every direction v, both f_w(x)=p(⟨w,x⟩) and d_{w,v}(x)=p′(⟨w,x⟩)⟨v,x⟩ belong to L²(γ). There exist simultaneous membership witnesses and a field D(w):E→L²(γ) of continuous real linear maps such that D(w)v is exactly the class of d_{w,v}. The actual feature-class map Φ(w)=[f_w] is fully Fréchet differentiable at every ambient w, with derivative D(w). No feature membership, derivative membership, domination, differentiability or operator bound is an input.
assumptions: E has real inner-product normed, finite-dimensional and Borel structures; no positive dimension is required.
p is any finite real polynomial, including zero, constant and non-even polynomials. The weight w ranges over all of E.

steps.title: Produce Gaussian radial domination
steps.text: Finite Gaussian norm moments and polynomial induction give L² radial envelopes on each bounded weight ball. Applying them to p and p′ times one radial factor produces the actual feature and directional-derivative memberships.
steps.formula: |p(\langle u,x\rangle)|\le B_0(x),\quad |p\prime(\langle u,x\rangle)|\,\|x\|\le B_1(x),\qquad B_0,B_1\in L^2(\gamma).
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Build the represented bounded linear map
steps.text: The directional scalar formula is linear in v. Its L² norm is bounded by an envelope norm times ‖v‖, so it extends directly to a continuous linear map with the required actual-class identity.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Differentiate the pointwise polynomial
steps.text: Polynomial differentiation composed with the inner-product functional yields the genuine scalar derivative for every x and every direction.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Control the normalized remainder locally
steps.text: A local scalar mean-value bound and the directional bound dominate the normalized scalar remainder by twice one L² envelope. At u=w define the inverse-norm normalization by the usual totalized value zero.
steps.formula: r_u(x)=p(\langle u,x\rangle)-p(\langle w,x\rangle)-p\prime(\langle w,x\rangle)\langle u-w,x\rangle,\quad q_u(x)=\|u-w\|^{-1}|r_u(x)|\le2B(x).
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Use dominated convergence on the squared remainder
steps.text: Pointwise Fréchet differentiability gives q_u(x)→0, and 4B² is integrable. Dominated convergence therefore controls the whole L² remainder, not just each fixed directional limit.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Identify the actual quotient norm
steps.text: Almost-everywhere identities for subtraction, scalar multiplication and toLp identify the displayed integral with the squared norm of the normalized genuine class remainder. Taking its square root proves the full ambient Fréchet limit.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

units.title: The same Gaussian derivative is bounded and Lipschitz on the closed unit ball
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Under the same finite-dimensional real inner-product, Borel and arbitrary finite-polynomial assumptions, there exist actual feature and directional-derivative L² membership witnesses and one continuous-linear derivative field D(w), with D(w)v=[p′(⟨w,·⟩)⟨v,·⟩] and Φ fully Fréchet differentiable with derivative D(w) at every ambient w. There also exist strictly positive real constants M₁,M₂ such that ‖D(w)‖op≤M₁ for every ‖w‖≤1 and ‖D(u)−D(w)‖op≤M₂‖u−w‖ whenever both weights lie in the closed unit ball. The constants may depend on p and the ambient space; no dimension-independent rate is asserted. All memberships, derivatives and bounds are produced.
assumptions: The only mathematical data are E with its finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures, and a finite real polynomial p.
The returned operator estimates apply to the same derivative field in the ambient derivative conclusion; both endpoint weights in the difference estimate satisfy norm at most one.

steps.text: Gaussian radial moments supply B,C∈L² uniformly on the closed unit ball, with radial factors of orders one and two respectively.

units.title: A Hilbert feature potential has a controlled tangent Riesz field
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let E,H be complete real inner-product normed spaces. Let F:E→H be a map, and let each D(w):E→H be a continuous real linear map satisfying the actual ambient identity DF(w)=D(w) for every w. Suppose M₁,M₂≥0, ‖D(w)‖op≤M₁ on the closed unit ball, and ‖D(w)−D(u)‖op≤M₂‖w−u‖ there. For r∈H define V_r(w)=2⟨r,F(w)⟩ and G_r(w)=2(D(w)*r−⟨D(w)*r,w⟩w), where * is the Hilbert adjoint. At every ambient w, V_r has derivative 2⟨D(w)*r,·⟩. At every unit w, G_r(w) is tangent, satisfies ⟨G_r(w),v⟩=2⟨r,D(w)v⟩ for every v perpendicular to w, and has norm at most 2M₁‖r‖. For all r,q and unit w,u, its joint increment is bounded by 2M₁‖r−q‖+2(M₂+2M₁)‖q‖‖w−u‖.
assumptions: E,H are complete real inner-product normed spaces. F and D have the explicit actual full ambient Fréchet derivative relation.
M₁,M₂ are nonnegative; uniform derivative and operator Lipschitz bounds are explicit inputs on the closed unit ball. The tangent and joint field bounds require unit endpoint weights.

steps.title: Control the orthogonal projection
steps.text: For unit w, expand the squared norm of P_wz. Subtracting a nonnegative squared normal component proves contraction.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Control projection movement
steps.text: Rewrite the projection difference into one change of vector direction and one change of its inner product. Cauchy–Schwarz and unit norms bound both terms.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Differentiate the scalar potential
steps.text: The chain rule for the bounded residual functional and the adjoint identity give the full ambient derivative. Projecting its representing vector removes only the normal part, which pairs to zero against every tangent direction.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Bound the tangent field
steps.text: Adjoints preserve operator norms; the projection is contractive. Multiplication by two gives the asserted residual-dependent bound.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Separate residual and location changes
steps.text: At a fixed w use linearity in r. For the fixed q location change, split the derivative-adjoint increment and the projection increment; combine the previous estimates.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

units.title: Actual Bochner means are controlled by the all-coupling quadratic cost
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let U be any measurable space and H a complete real normed vector space. Let K:U→H be strongly measurable with ‖K(u)‖≤B. Let c:U×U→ℝ be measurable with 0≤c(z)≤C, and suppose ‖K(u)−K(v)‖≤L c(u,v), where B,C,L≥0. For any two probability measures μ,ν on U, define Q as the infimum, over all actual couplings π with these two marginals, of ∫c² dπ, interpreted as an extended nonnegative integral; set W=Q^(1/2). Then K is genuinely Bochner integrable under each law, Q is finite, and ‖∫K dμ−∫K dν‖≤L W.toReal. For every y∈H both residual norms are at most B+‖y‖. No optimizer, chosen-plan bound, finite-cost assumption or mean-identity premise is supplied. U need not carry a vector-space structure, and c need not be a metric.
assumptions: U is measurable; H is a complete real normed vector space. μ and ν are actual probability measures.
K is strongly measurable and bounded by the nonnegative B. c is jointly measurable, nonnegative and bounded by nonnegative C.
L≥0 and the displayed feature increment bound holds for every pair; symmetry, a triangle inequality and an optimal coupling are not assumptions.

steps.title: Produce integrability and finite transport cost
steps.text: Strong measurability and the global norm bound give both Bochner integrals. The actual product probability μ⊗ν is a feasible coupling and has cost at most C², so Q is finite before toReal is used.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Use the actual marginals for every coupling
steps.text: Every feasible coupling is a probability. Marginal pushforward identities and Bochner subtraction express the actual mean difference as one integral of feature increments.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Square the integral bound
steps.text: The feature increment hypothesis first bounds the mean norm by L∫c dπ. Nonnegativity of ∫(c−∫c)² gives the probability square-integral inequality, without an assumed cost estimate.
steps.formula: \left(\int c\,d\pi\right)^2\le\int c^2\,d\pi,\qquad A^2\le L^2\int c^2\,d\pi,\quad A=\left\|\int K\,d\mu-\int K\,d\nu\right\|.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Take the infimum over all feasible costs
steps.text: For L>0, the same lower bound (A/L)² lies below every actual coupling cost. The order characterization of the extended-real infimum therefore places it below Q; no attainment or optimizer is used.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Handle the square root and the zero constant
steps.text: Finiteness justifies the real conversion and the square-root identity. If L=0, the product-coupling squared bound already gives A=0 and no division is performed.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Bound both residuals
steps.text: The norm of each actual mean is at most B. The triangle inequality gives the two bounds for the same arbitrary fixed y.
steps.lean: The exact implementation is available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.
